children: Brent crude prices rose toward $105 per barrel on Monday, marking a third consecutive session of gains after deadly attacks on Riyadh's airport prompted President Trump to consider joining Saudi Arabia in retaliating against Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, raising fears of a broader regional conflict that could further disrupt global energy supplies.
Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport was targeted again on Sunday by Iran-backed Houthi militants, a day after an earlier strike killed 12 people and injured more than 300.
Meanwhile, a drone struck a tanker near the Sohar anchorage off Oman over the weekend, just outside the Strait of Hormuz.
Separately, Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an “energy ceasefire” that would take effect immediately.

In the US, the Department of Energy announced approval of an emergency exchange involving up to 4 million barrels of crude oil from strategic reserves to help mitigate supply disruptions caused by Hurricane Isaias.

title: Brent Edges Higher on Saudi Airport Attack
